sections.heading: Destination Snapshot
sections.body: Magic Wood is compact Swiss gneiss bouldering in a steep forest valley: over 1,000 problems, hard classics, short links between sectors and conditions that can feel world class when the air is cool and dry.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Magic Wood is small on the map and big in reputation. The boulders sit in forest above the Hinterrhein, giving the area a concentrated feel: you can move between objectives quickly, but the climbing rarely feels easy.

The destination is best known for hard bouldering, yet there are problems across a wider spread. The trick is choosing problems and conditions intelligently rather than assuming the forest will hand out grades.

sections.heading: History
sections.body:
Magic Wood became famous because a compact valley produced a remarkable density of quality gneiss problems. It is now one of Europe’s standard references for hard forest bouldering.

That popularity makes low-impact behaviour important. Stay on paths, respect camping and parking rules, and avoid turning a small valley into a crowded gym.

sections.heading: Rock and Style
sections.body:
The rock is Swiss gneiss, with overhangs, crimps, slabs and powerful compression. Many problems are physical, but good footwork still matters.

The forest can hold moisture. When conditions are dry, the rock feels crisp and positive; when humidity rises, hard problems can turn quickly.

sections.heading: Who Is It For
sections.body:
Magic Wood is best for boulderers who already enjoy outdoor problem solving. Strong climbers will recognize many classics, but intermediates can still build a good trip by choosing carefully.

Beginners should come with realistic expectations, enough pads and partners who can manage landings and sector choice.

sections.heading: Grades and Scale
sections.body:
Magic Wood has more than 1,000 boulder problems in a compact area of roughly one square kilometre. There is no single clean grade span that captures the area well.

Treat Magic Wood as quality-dense rather than easy-dense. A current topo is essential for finding the right circuits and warm-ups.

sections.heading: Season
sections.body:
Spring and autumn are the best-supported planning seasons. Summer can work in shade when humidity is acceptable, while winter is usually a poor choice because of seepage and wet conditions.

For any season, dry rock is the real filter.

sections.heading: Gear
sections.body:
Bring multiple pads, a brush, tape, warm layers and a current topo. Landings vary, and many worthwhile lines climb better with a thoughtful pad stack.

Skin management matters. The gneiss can be sharp enough to end a trip early if you ignore it.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body:
A car is the practical transport plan for Magic Wood. The valley setting makes arrival, food runs and weather pivots easier with independent transport.

Check current parking and camping arrangements before arrival, as local rules can change.

sections.heading: Stay and Eat
sections.body:
Plan around campsite and guesthouse-style bases. Keep the plan flexible and current because Magic Wood's local camping and access setup is an important part of trip logistics.

Choose lodging that lets the group rest properly; the climbing is intense enough without poor recovery.

sections.heading: Rest Days
sections.body: Rest days can be quiet: river walks, valley views, food runs and skin recovery. The area is compact, so leaving the pads behind is sometimes the smartest decision you make all week.

sections.heading: Tips and Ethics
sections.body:
Warm up patiently and save skin. Magic Wood has enough famous hard lines to make climbers rush, but the best days come from building into the conditions.

Respect paths, camping rules and other groups. The area’s compactness is a strength only if everyone keeps impact low.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body:
Uneven landings, powerful moves and damp rock are the main concerns. Use enough pads, spot actively and avoid climbing when holds are seeping or wet.

Many problems are close together, so stay aware of pads, people and fall zones around busy classics.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Magic Wood only for strong climbers? No, but its reputation and density are strongest for committed boulderers.

How many problems are there? More than 1,000.

When should I go? Spring and autumn are the safest planning windows.
